content.title: Tax Day 2026 Deals: Free Food, Discounts And Other ‘Tax Relief’
content.text: This tax season, Blue Buffalo, is giving dog parents the “write off” they deserve on Tax Day. The brand is one of many offering deals and promos on April 15.Blue BuffaloReady to file your tax return? While Tax Day often means settling up with the IRS, it also comes with a small consolation prize: a wave of deals, freebies, and promotions that have turned April 15 into a shopping and dining event. From discounted meals to tax-themed giveaways, brands are offering a little “relief” of their own—no forms or schedules required.More deals are expected to pop up as the deadline approaches, so check back often, especially around lunch and happy hour on April 15. New additions will be marked with (NEW) to help you find them quickly.Here’s what’s on tap so far:Food and DrinkBJ’s Restaurant & Brewhouse. BJ’s Restaurant and Brewhouse is celebrating Tax Day by offering $10 off any $40 order for takeout or delivery orders on April 15. Dickey’s Barbecue Pit. Dickey’s Barbecue Pit is helping guests turn Tax Day into a tasty write-off with $10 off orders of $50 or more using code WRITEOFF. The online-exclusive deal is available on dickeys.com and the Dickey’s app on Tuesday, April 14 and Wednesday, April 15 at all locations nationwide.Fazoli’s. Rewards members at Fazoli’s can get a buy-one-get-one-free Baked Spaghetti deal at participating locations on April 15. Great American Cookies. On Tax Day, Great American Cookies loyalty members can buy one cookie cake slice and get one free at participating locations (in-store only).Grimaldi’s Pizzeria. On April 15, guests can enjoy $10.40 off any purchase of $40 or more all day (dine-in, to-go, and online with code TAXDAY26). The offer applies across the menu, is valid at most Grimaldi’s locations (excluding Brooklyn and Las Vegas Palazzo), and cannot be combined with other offers. Grubhub. Grubhub is helping diners ease their “Taxiety” with the Grubhub Fee Return – giving back $100,000 in Grubhub credit to diners who paid fees on food delivery apps in 2025. Users can also score $10.40 off $50+ orders from select partners like Sweetgreen, Krispy Kreme, and Chili’s, or $10 off a first order with code FEERETURN10 (for more info, check out the company’s Tax Day themed webpage). Jersey Mike’s. Jersey Mike's is relaunching the Boardwalk Bundle for a limited time on April 13. The deal starts at $10.99 (a nod to Form 1099). It includes a regular #2 sub, chips, and a drink and isn’t valid for delivery. (NEW) Kentucky Fried Chicken. Recent data shows Americans living alone spend an average of $10,470 more per year - the so-called “singles tax.” KFC’s Box Feasts (a full meal starts at $7) is, the company says, exactly the kind of math people want on Tax Day. Single people might pay more for everything else… just not for dinner.Kona Ice. Call it a palate cleanser for your tax stress. The brand’s annual “Chill Out Day” returns with free shaved ice at participating locations. No purchase necessary, just track down the truck. Krispy Kreme. On Wednesday, April 15 only, guests can mark “taxes done” by receiving a free Original Glazed® dozen when they purchase any dozen doughnuts at regular price in shop or drive-thru, limit two dozen per guest. Guests who order any dozen online at regular price for pickup or delivery can use the promo code “TAXBREAK” to receive an Original Glazed dozen for FREE! Limit one free dozen when ordering online via Krispy Kreme’s app or website.Kroger. Kroger is serving up a limited-time deal to help readers focus on crunching the numbers and not their dinner budget. Starting on Tax Day, April 15 through Wednesday, April 22, customers can write off the stress of mealtime with a Buy One, Get One 50% off deal on Private Selection frozen meals. The offer is valid on Private Selection’s new, globally inspired dishes—meeting tax filing deadlines has never been more delicious with these restaurant-inspired classics. (NEW) Miami Grill. Miami Grill is offering a $7.99 Chicken Pita + Fries special on April 15, giving guests an affordable, satisfying meal option to end tax season.Paris Baguette. With Tax Day right around the corner, Paris Baguette is giving guests a reason to treat themselves with a free pastry offer, just in time to enjoy alongside its new Korean BBQ menu and refreshing mint lemonades for spring. PB Rewards members can enjoy a free pastry with any beverage purchase on Tax Day (April 15), perfect for pairing with the brand’s latest menu additions. Pizza Hut. On April 15th, pizza lovers can score a crave-worthy large 3-topping pizza starting at just $10* on a choice of one of three iconic crusts: the new and improved Hand Tossed, Tavern Style, or Thin 'N Crispy. Just head over to your local Pizza Hut, PizzaHut.com or the Pizza Hut app to claim your slice of the savings. (*Limited time offer at select participating locations only. Additional charge for Original Stuffed Crust®, Pan, or extra cheese/toppings. Priced higher in some locations, including CA. Taxes, tip, and delivery fees not included. Exclusions apply.)Potbelly is offering a double toasty-hot opportunity to write off the stress of Tax Day.PotbellyPotbelly. On April 15, Potbelly fans can enjoy a free Original-size sandwich or wrap with the purchase of any Big or Original-size sandwich or wrap. It’s a double-toasty-hot opportunity to write off the day's stress and cash in on something craveable. Fans can access this promotion through the Potbelly app or on Potbelly.com by using the promo code ‘BOGO’ at checkout. QDOBA. From Monday, April 20, through Sunday, April 26, QDOBA Rewards members can get $5 off any full-sized entrée. Guests can visit www.TaxDayGuacRelief.com by Wednesday, April 15 at 11:59 pm ET, then a $5 off reward will be dropped into their rewards wallet on April 20. The offer is exclusive to QDOBA Rewards members.Round Table Pizza. Guests can enjoy 15% off all orders (valid for dine-in, carryout or delivery) from April 15–19 with code RTP978 at participating locations, because everyone deserves a pizza break after crunching numbers!Shipley Do-Nuts. Shipley Donuts is offering a half-dozen glazed donuts for $4.15, available through Wednesday 4/15. Offer valid in-story only and limited to one reward per guest. Smoothie King. Waited until the last minute to file your taxes? Smoothie King is here to help you power through and meet your deadline. On April 15th only, Smoothie King is offering $3 off when you join Healthy Rewards by downloading the Smoothie King app. Subway. On Tax Day, Subway is rewarding Sub Club members with a special offer: FREE footlong sandwich with the purchase of another footlong. And, because filing your 1040 form is no fun, 1,040 lucky guests who purchase a sandwich on April 15 will receive a full refund on their entire order, getting both footlong sandwiches completely FREE. It's Subway's way of helping customers tackle one of the toughest financial moments of the year with a delicious break. The BOGO offer is available through April 28 via the Subway app or website using promo code FLBOGO.Travelin' Tom's Coffee will also celebrate Chill Out Day.Travelin' Tom's CoffeeTravelin' Tom's Coffee. Travelin' Tom's Coffee (the sister company of Kona Ice) will also celebrate Chill Out Day on April 15. Participating Travelin' Tom's trucks will give away free frozen beverages.(NEW) Wendy’s. This Wednesday, April 15, Wendy's is offering fans FREE 6pc Nuggets with a $5 purchase via the Wendy’s app. It's their way of celebrating the end of tax season – a delicious recognition for getting to the other side. Ziggi’s Coffee. On Tuesday, April 15, guests who make an in-store purchase at participating Ziggi’s Coffee locations will receive a $2 Bounce Back coupon to use on their next visit while supplies last - no sign-ups, no app, no extra steps. Designed to bring a small moment of relief (and reward) to an otherwise stressful day, the offer encourages guests to treat themselves now and enjoy another visit the following week. The Bounce Back coupon is valid April 16–22, 2026, encouraging a return visit and extending the Tax Day moment beyond a single day.7-Eleven. 7-Eleven is offering $10.40 on any 7NOW Delivery order of $25 or more when you use promo code WRITEOFF at checkout. Offer valid on April 15 only. Quirky Promotions and OffersBlue Buffalo. Dependents, but fluffier. Blue Buffalo has launched the Love Made Fresh Dog Tax Credit, giving dog parents the chance to “write off” the cost of food, treats, toys and all the things that make a happy home. Ahead of Tax Day, dog parents can go to BlueBuffaloDogTaxCredit.com to “claim” their pup as a dog-pendent for the chance to receive a $1,000 credit to put toward Love Made Fresh, Blue Buffalo’s new fresh dog food offering.(This isn’t just a quirky promo—you can read a real life story about a pet owner who sued the IRS to claim her dog as a dependent here.)Goldfish. Do you take Goldfish crackers from your kids and call it a “parent tax”? Starting at 4:15 p.m. ET on April 15, parents can “file” their return at GoldfishParentTax.com, answering a few questions about their household Goldfish consumption. If eligible, families will receive a refund of two bags of free Goldfish crackers, while supplies last.This Tax Day, Goldfish® is introducing the Goldfish Parent Tax Return, a playful way to pay back all those Goldfish that ‘mysteriously disappear’.Goldfish Non-Food Deals and Practical Perks Office Depot / OfficeMax. You can benefit from free document shredding services around Tax Day. It’s the financial equivalent of opening a window after a long winter—clear out the old paperwork and pretend you’ve always been this organized. You’ll need a coupon, available on the company’s website. Straight Talk Wireless. “Tax season is free phone season.” This tax season, new and existing customers can start fresh with a new phone and real unlimited data. Taxes and fees apply. Plan purchase required for offer. Limit of two phones per customer. SmartPay purchases excluded. Not available on family plans.TurboTax (in connection with Southwest Rapid Rewards). Eligible filers can score Rapid Rewards bonus points for filing their taxes using TurboTax. It’s less instant gratification and more “future you will enjoy this,” which is about as on-brand as Tax Day gets. (Eligibility requirements apply.)More InfoThese deals, discounts, and freebies are based on information provided by companies and their representatives, as well as social media. While every effort has been made to ensure accuracy, I haven’t personally visited each location or verified every offer. Keep in mind that many of these businesses are independently owned franchises, so participation and promotions may vary by location.Some offers may require a coupon, app download, rewards membership, or engagement on social media. When in doubt, check the company’s website or social channels for the most up-to-date details (links have been included where available).As always, be sure to read the fine print. If you have questions about a specific promotion, it’s best to contact the company directly.Wishing you an easy Tax Day!ForbesForbes Last Minute Tax Guide: How To Navigate The Changes On Your 2025 Return
